Title: August 13, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session

Topic1.Title: Special Meeting: Executive Session on Potential New Litigation
Topic1.Summary: The council unanimously approved a motion to convene an executive session under C.R.S. 24-6-402(4) and City Charter Section 21A2 to receive confidential legal advice on potential new litigation. The city attorney confirmed the meeting notice met Colorado law and the charter. The council reconvened in public after the executive session, which included the city manager, attorney, and council members, and the special meeting was closed at 6:01 p.m.

Topic2.Title: Study Session: Strategic Planning Check-In
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the process for developing the 2027-2030 citywide strategic plan, which will include several community and council touchpoints over five months. The presentation described a 'world of possibilities' document of roughly 41 inputs drawn from about 170 staff proposals, and explained how a prioritization rubric was used to score them. Council members asked how the tool works, how budget and outcome data from the existing plan will be used, how community input is incorporated, and how the plan will connect to the comprehensive plan and annual work planning. Several members stressed the need for earlier council involvement, safety and maintenance planning, and clearer prioritization of core services.

Topic3.Title: Civic Area East Bookend Development Partnership RFP
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented the goals and process for a request for proposals to select a private development partner for the East Bookend of the Civic Area, with the West Bookend as an optional component. The stated goals include creating a food destination anchored by the Boulder County Farmers Market, integrating recreation with Boulder Creek Park, incorporating arts and culture, generating revenue through sales or leases, and reducing the city's property management burden. Staff reported that nine responses to the prior request for interest supported a partnership model, and the RFP is expected in late summer 2026 with selection in early 2027. Council members asked about selection committee membership, safety and activation, ongoing park operating costs, phasing, funding, and the Arboretum Path, and several suggested clearer goal language.

Topic4.Title: 2026 State and County Ballot Measures
Topic4.Summary: Staff reviewed the Boulder County early childhood care and education mill levy and eight qualified state ballot measures, along with several measures pending signature verification, and explained how the council can adopt an official city position by resolution. Staff noted that council is not required to take positions and identified potential city impacts for each measure. Council members reached consensus to direct staff to draft opposition resolutions on five measures, including the fentanyl penalties measure, the law enforcement reporting measure, the gender-related sports and surgery measures, and the restore our roads measure, and support resolutions on the Boulder County child care measure, the graduated income tax, the sporting goods tax for conservation, and the education funding measure, with the sporting goods tax item receiving only partial support.
